label: thm:LN_main
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:LN_main}
Let $\hbar>0$ and $\rho_0>0$.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item (Balls) Along the standard sequence of balls $\{\mathcal B_K\}$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:LN_packing} (which depends on $\rho_0$), the limit $\lim_{K\to\infty}e^\hbar_\mathrm{Jel}(\rho_0,\mathcal B_K)$ exists.
\item (General domains) For every LN-admissible sequence $\{\Omega_N\}$, the limit
\[
\boxed{e^\hbar_\mathrm{Jel}(\rho_0):=\lim_{N\to\infty}e^\hbar_\mathrm{Jel}(\rho_0,\Omega_N)}
\]
exists and is equal to the limit in item~(i). In particular, it does not depend on the shape of the domains.
\item (Scaling) $e^\hbar_\mathrm{Jel}(\rho_0)=\rho_0^{4/3}\,\tilde e_\mathrm{Jel}\big(\hbar^2\rho_0^{1/3}\big)$, where $\tilde e_\mathrm{Jel}(\lambda):=e^{\sqrt\lambda}_\mathrm{Jel}(1)$, $\lambda>0$, is the energy at unit density.
\item (Regularity) $\lambda\mapsto \tilde e_\mathrm{Jel}(\lambda)$ is concave and non-decreasing on $(0,\infty)$, hence continuous. Therefore $\rho_0\mapsto e^\hbar_\mathrm{Jel}(\rho_0)$ is continuous on $(0,\infty)$. Moreover, for a fixed LN-admissible sequence at unit density, the convergence $e^{\sqrt\lambda}_\mathrm{Jel}(1,\Omega_N)\to \tilde e_\mathrm{Jel}(\lambda)$ is locally uniform in $\lambda\in(0,\infty)$.
\end{enumerate}

name: Jellium

label: thm:UEG
title: Theorem
head: environment

label: rem:UEG_vs_Jel
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:UEG_vs_Jel}
It is noted in~\cite[Sec.~2.2]{lewin2020local} that $e_\mathrm{UEG}$ ``is believed to be the same as the ground state energy of Jellium''. In the classical case, the equality $e_\mathrm{UEG}=e_\mathrm{Jel}$ has been proved~\cite{lewin2019floating,cotar2017equality}; in the quantum case the equality was open. The inequality $\tilde e_\mathrm{UEG}(\lambda)\geqslant\tilde e^{\rm GC}_\mathrm{Jel}(\lambda)$ is proved in~\cite[proof of Thm.~5.1, Step~4]{lewin2018statistical}, where $\tilde e^{\rm GC}_\mathrm{Jel}(\lambda)$ is the thermodynamic limit of grand-canonical Jellium, with free particle number and without confinement to the support of the background. This energy is attributed there to~\cite{lieb1975thermodynamic}, but~\cite{lieb1975thermodynamic} treats the canonical Jellium with Dirichlet boundary conditions and does not prove the identification of the two limits. Theorem~\ref{thm:lower} proves the inequality for the Jellium energy of Theorem~\ref{thm:LN_main}.

label: rem:main_consequences
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:main_consequences}
By Theorem~\ref{thm:main}, the properties of $\tilde e_\mathrm{UEG}$ in Theorem~\ref{thm:UEG}(iii)--(vi) hold for the Jellium energy of Theorem~\ref{thm:LN_main}. In particular, $\tilde e_\mathrm{Jel}(\lambda)=c_\mathrm{TF}\lambda-c_{\mathrm D}+o(1)$ as $\lambda\to\infty$, and $\tilde e_\mathrm{Jel}(\lambda)\to e_\mathrm{UEG}$ as $\lambda\to0$, where $e_\mathrm{UEG}$ is the classical UEG energy of~\cite[Thm.~2.6]{lewin2018statistical}. The latter coincides with the classical Jellium energy~\cite{lewin2019floating,cotar2017equality}. The general shape of $e^\hbar_\mathrm{UEG}(\rho_0)=e^\hbar_\mathrm{Jel}(\rho_0)$ as a function of $\rho_0$ is sketched in Figure~\ref{fig:energy_shape}.

title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:basic_lieb_oxford}
There is a universal constant $c_{\rm LO}>0$ such that every grand-canonical state ${\bm{\Gamma}}$ with $\rho_{{\bm{\Gamma}}}\in L^1\cap L^{4/3}(\mathbb{R}^3)$ satisfies
\[
\mathcal{C}({\bm{\Gamma}})-D(\rho_{{\bm{\Gamma}}})\geqslant-c_{\rm LO}\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}\rho_{{\bm{\Gamma}}}^{4/3}.
\]

name: Lieb--Oxford

label: lem:basic_elementary
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:basic_elementary}
The following hold true.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ be measurable, and let $\eta\geqslant0$ satisfy $\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}\eta=1$ and $\sqrt\eta\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^3)$. Then $0\leqslant\mathbb{1}_\Omega*\eta\leqslant1$ and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:basic_sqrt_cutoff}
|\nabla\sqrt{\mathbb{1}_\Omega*\eta}|^2
\leqslant\mathbb{1}_\Omega*|\nabla\sqrt\eta|^2
\leqslant\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}|\nabla\sqrt\eta|^2
\quad\hbox{a.e.}
\end{equation}
In particular, $\sqrt{\mathbb{1}_\Omega*\eta}\in W^{1,\infty}(\mathbb{R}^3)$. If $\rho\geqslant0$ and $\sqrt\rho\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^3)$, then $\sqrt{(\mathbb{1}_\Omega*\eta)\rho}\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^3)$ and
\[
\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}|\nabla\sqrt{(\mathbb{1}_\Omega*\eta)\rho}|^2
\leqslant2\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}|\nabla\sqrt\rho|^2
+2\|\nabla\sqrt{\mathbb{1}_\Omega*\eta}\|_\infty^2\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}\rho.
\]
\item Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain, and let $\eta$ satisfy the assumptions in~(i), with $\operatorname{supp}\eta\subset B_1$. Set $\eta_\delta(x)=\delta^{-3}\eta(x/\delta)$. Then
\[
\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}|\nabla\sqrt{\mathbb{1}_\Omega*\eta_\delta}|^2
\leqslant C\frac{|\partial\Omega|}{\delta}
\]
for all sufficiently small $\delta>0$, where $|\partial\Omega|=\mathcal H^2(\partial\Omega)$ is the surface area and $C$ depends only on $\eta$ and the Lipschitz geometry of $\Omega$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

label: thm:basic_newton
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:basic_newton}
Let $f\in L^1(\mathbb{R}^3)$ be radial about $a\in\mathbb{R}^3$ and supported in $\overline{B_r(a)}$, and write $f(s)$ for its value at distance $s$ from $a$. Then, for $x\ne a$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:basic_newton}
\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}\frac{f(y)}{|x-y|}\,\mathrm dy=\frac1{|x-a|}\int_0^{|x-a|}f(s)s^2\,\mathrm ds+\int_{|x-a|}^\infty f(s)s\,\mathrm ds.
\end{equation}
Consequently:
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item For $|x-a|\geqslant r$,
\[
\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}\frac{f(y)}{|x-y|}\,\mathrm dy=\frac1{|x-a|}\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}f.
\]
If $\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}f=0$, the left side vanishes outside $B_r(a)$, and $D(f,g)=0$ for every $g\in L^1(\mathbb{R}^3)$ supported outside $B_r(a)$.
\item If $f\geqslant0$, then $\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}f(y)|x-y|^{-1}\,\mathrm dy\leqslant|x-a|^{-1}\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}f$ for all $x\ne a$.
\item If $g\in L^1(\mathbb{R}^3)$ is radial about $b\in\mathbb{R}^3$ and supported in a closed ball $\overline{B_{r'}(b)}$ disjoint from $\overline{B_r(a)}$, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:basic_radial_cross}
2D(f,g)=\frac1{|a-b|}\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}f\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}g.
\end{equation}
\item If $f$ is bounded, then
\[
D(f)=\frac12\int_0^\infty\frac1{s^2}\Big(\int_{B_s(a)}f\Big)^2\,\mathrm ds.
\]
\end{enumerate}

label: lem:basic_onsager
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Onsager

title: Proof
body_md:
For $\nu=\sum_j\mu_j-\rho$,
\[
D(\nu)=\sum_jD(\mu_j)+2\sum_{j<k}D(\mu_j,\mu_k)-2\sum_jD(\mu_j,\rho)+D(\rho).
\]
The uniform probability measure on a ball of radius $a$ has $D(\mu_j)=\frac3{5a}$. By Theorem~\ref{thm:basic_newton}(ii), the potential of $\mu_j$ is at most $|x-x_j|^{-1}$, so $2D(\mu_j,\mu_k)\leqslant|x_j-x_k|^{-1}$. For the background term, let $\mu_a:=|B_a|^{-1}\mathbb{1}_{B_a(0)}$. The function $|z|^{-1}-\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}\mu_a(y)|z-y|^{-1}\,\mathrm dy$ is nonnegative by Theorem~\ref{thm:basic_newton}(ii) and vanishes for $|z|\geqslant a$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:basic_newton}(i). Hence
\begin{align*}
\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}\frac{\rho(y)}{|x_j-y|}\,\mathrm dy-2D(\mu_j,\rho)
&=\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}\rho(x_j-z)\Big(\frac1{|z|}-\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}\frac{\mu_a(y)}{|z-y|}\,\mathrm dy\Big)\,\mathrm dz\\
&\leqslant\bar\rho\int_{B_a}\Big(\frac1{|z|}-\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}\frac{\mu_a(y)}{|z-y|}\,\mathrm dy\Big)\,\mathrm dz
=\frac{2\pi}5\bar\rho a^2.
\end{align*}
Inserting these three facts into the expansion of $D(\nu)$ gives the claim, and $D(\nu)\geqslant0$ gives the last assertion.

label: lem:lower_completion
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:lower_completion}
Fix $\rho_0>0$ and $C_0>0$. There exist constants $h,C_1>0$, depending only on $\rho_0$ and $C_0$, such that
whenever  $\ell\geqslant1$ and a normalized $N$-particle state $\Gamma_N$ supported in $B_\ell$ with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions verifies the bound
\[
\mathcal J_{\rho_0\mathbb{1}_{B_\ell}}(\Gamma_N)\leqslant C_0\ell^3,
\]
there exist a radius $\ell'\in[\ell,\ell+h]$ with $M=\rho_0|B_{\ell'}|\in\mathbb{N}$ (neutrality) and a normalized $M$-particle state $\Gamma_M$ supported in $B_{\ell'}$ satisfying homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:lower_completion}
\mathcal J_{\rho_0\mathbb{1}_{B_{\ell'}}}(\Gamma_M)
\leqslant\mathcal J_{\rho_0\mathbb{1}_{B_\ell}}(\Gamma_N)+C_1\ell^2.
\end{equation}

name: Neutralization in a slightly larger ball

label: thm:lower
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:lower}
$e_\mathrm{Jel}(\rho_0)\leqslant e_\mathrm{UEG}(\rho_0)$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Choose a radial smoothing function $\chi\geqslant0$ with $\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}\chi=1$, $\operatorname{supp}\chi\subset B_1$ and $\sqrt\chi\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^3)$. For $\ell\to\infty$, put
\[
\delta_\ell=\ell^{-1/2},\qquad r_\ell=\ell-2\delta_\ell.
\]
The conditions $\delta_\ell/r_\ell\to0$ and $\delta_\ell r_\ell\to\infty$ allow us to apply Theorem~\ref{thm:UEG}(ii). Since $|B_{r_\ell}|/|B_\ell|\to1$, we obtain
\[
E\big(\rho_0\mathbb{1}_{B_{r_\ell}}*\chi_{\delta_\ell}\big)=e_\mathrm{UEG}(\rho_0)|B_\ell|+o(\ell^3).
\]
By~\cite[Thm.~4]{lewin2019universal}, the infimum defining $F_{\rm LL}(\rho_0\mathbb{1}_{B_{r_\ell}}*\chi_{\delta_\ell})$ is attained. Let ${\bm{\Gamma}}_\ell$ be a minimizer, so that $\rho_{{\bm{\Gamma}}_\ell}=\rho_0\mathbb{1}_{B_{r_\ell}}*\chi_{\delta_\ell}$ and $\mathcal{E}({\bm{\Gamma}}_\ell)=E(\rho_{{\bm{\Gamma}}_\ell})$ by~\eqref{eq:UEG_E}. Clearly, $\operatorname{supp}\rho_{{\bm{\Gamma}}_\ell}\subset B_{\ell-\delta_\ell}$.

The density satisfies $0\leqslant\rho_{{\bm{\Gamma}}_\ell}\leqslant\rho_0\mathbb{1}_{B_\ell}$ and $\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}\rho_{{\bm{\Gamma}}_\ell}=\rho_0|B_{r_\ell}|$. Consequently, for $f_\ell=\rho_{{\bm{\Gamma}}_\ell}-\rho_0\mathbb{1}_{B_\ell}$,
\begin{align*}
\|f_\ell\|_1&=\rho_0(|B_\ell|-|B_{r_\ell}|)\leqslant C\ell^2\delta_\ell,
\qquad \|f_\ell\|_\infty\leqslant\rho_0,\\
D(f_\ell)&\leqslant C(\ell^2\delta_\ell)^{5/3}=C\ell^{5/2}=o(\ell^3),
\end{align*}
where we used $D(f)\leqslant D(|f|)\leqslant C\|f\|_1^{5/3}\|f\|_\infty^{1/3}$ for real $f\in L^1\cap L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^3)$. Combining this with the identity~\eqref{eq:conj_identity} gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:lower_trial}
\mathcal J_{\rho_0\mathbb{1}_{B_\ell}}({\bm{\Gamma}}_\ell)
=e_\mathrm{UEG}(\rho_0)|B_\ell|+o(\ell^3).
\end{equation}
Set $p_n=\Tr\Gamma_\ell^{(n)}$. Since ${\bm{\Gamma}}\mapsto \mathcal J_\zeta({\bm{\Gamma}})$ is affine for fixed $\zeta$ we obtain
\[
\mathcal J_{\rho_0\mathbb{1}_{B_\ell}}({\bm{\Gamma}}_\ell)=\sum_{n:\,p_n>0}p_n\,\mathcal J_{\rho_0\mathbb{1}_{B_\ell}}\big(\Gamma_\ell^{(n)}/p_n\big),\qquad\sum_n p_n=1,
\]
so the left side of~\eqref{eq:lower_trial} is an average of the Jellium energies of the normalized sectors.
Hence there is $N_\ell$ with $p_{N_\ell}>0$ such that the $N_\ell$-particle state $\Gamma_{N_\ell}=\Gamma_\ell^{(N_\ell)}/p_{N_\ell}$ satisfies $\mathcal J_{\rho_0\mathbb{1}_{B_\ell}}(\Gamma_{N_\ell})\leqslant\mathcal J_{\rho_0\mathbb{1}_{B_\ell}}({\bm{\Gamma}}_\ell)$.

Next, we check the hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{lem:lower_completion}. Since ${\bm{\Gamma}}_\ell$ has finite kinetic energy and its density vanishes outside $B_{\ell-\delta_\ell}$, every occupied sector has finite kinetic energy and is supported in this smaller ball. In particular, $\Gamma_{N_\ell}$ satisfies homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions in $B_\ell$. Fix $C_0=1+|B_1||e_\mathrm{UEG}(\rho_0)|$.
By~\eqref{eq:lower_trial} and the choice of $N_\ell$, for all sufficiently large $\ell$ we have
\[
\mathcal J_{\rho_0\mathbb{1}_{B_\ell}}(\Gamma_{N_\ell})
\leqslant\mathcal J_{\rho_0\mathbb{1}_{B_\ell}}({\bm{\Gamma}}_\ell)
\leqslant C_0\ell^3.
\]
Thus Lemma~\ref{lem:lower_completion} applies with the same $\rho_0$ and $C_0$ for all these $\ell$. It provides constants $h,C_1>0$ independent of $\ell$ and, for each $\ell$, a radius $\ell'\in[\ell,\ell+h]$ with $M_\ell=\rho_0|B_{\ell'}|\in\mathbb{N}$ and a normalized $M_\ell$-particle state $\Gamma_{M_\ell}$ supported in $B_{\ell'}$ satisfying homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions. This is a trial state for the canonical neutral Jellium problem in $B_{\ell'}$, so the variational principle and~\eqref{eq:lower_completion} give
\begin{align*}
E_\mathrm{Jel}(\rho_0,B_{\ell'})
&\leqslant\mathcal J_{\rho_0\mathbb{1}_{B_{\ell'}}}(\Gamma_{M_\ell})\\
&\leqslant\mathcal J_{\rho_0\mathbb{1}_{B_\ell}}(\Gamma_{N_\ell})+C_1\ell^2\\
&\leqslant\mathcal J_{\rho_0\mathbb{1}_{B_\ell}}({\bm{\Gamma}}_\ell)+C_1\ell^2\\
&=e_\mathrm{UEG}(\rho_0)|B_\ell|+o(\ell^3).
\end{align*}
Here the last line uses~\eqref{eq:lower_trial} and $C_1\ell^2=o(\ell^3)$, since $C_1$ is independent of $\ell$. Moreover, $0\leqslant\ell'-\ell\leqslant h$ implies $\ell'/\ell\to1$. Dividing by $|B_{\ell'}|$ therefore gives
\[
\frac{E_\mathrm{Jel}(\rho_0,B_{\ell'})}{|B_{\ell'}|}
\leqslant e_\mathrm{UEG}(\rho_0)\left(\frac\ell{\ell'}\right)^3+o(1).
\]
The left side tends to $e_\mathrm{Jel}(\rho_0)$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:LN_main}(ii) applied to the neutral balls $B_{\ell'}$ (Remark~\ref{rem:LN_balls}), while the right side tends to $e_\mathrm{UEG}(\rho_0)$. This proves the claim.

label: lem:upper_bounded_layer
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:upper_bounded_layer}
Fix $\rho_0>0$ and $\Lambda\geqslant1$. For all sufficiently large $\ell>0$, let $\delta'=\delta'(\ell)\geqslant0$ be the width of the transition layer, and let $\rho_\ell\geqslant 0$ satisfy $\sqrt{\rho_\ell}\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^3)$ and
\[
0\leqslant\rho_\ell\leqslant \Lambda\rho_0\mathbb{1}_{C_\ell+B_{\delta'}},
\qquad
\rho_\ell=\rho_0\quad\hbox{a.e.\ on }C_\ell\setminus(\partial C_\ell+B_{\delta'}).
\]
If $\delta'/\ell\to0$ as $\ell\to\infty$, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:upper_bounded_layer}
e_\mathrm{UEG}(\rho_0)\leqslant \liminf_{\ell\to\infty}\frac{E(\rho_\ell)}{\ell^3}.
\end{equation}

name: A bounded transition layer

title: Proof

label: lem:upper_collar
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:upper_collar}
Fix $\delta>0$ and $r\geqslant2\delta$. There exists a bounded radial function $g_{r,\delta}$ supported in $\overline{B_{r+2\delta}\setminus B_r}$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:upper_collar_charge}
\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}g_{r,\delta}=0,
\qquad
0\leqslant\rho_0+g_{r,\delta}\leqslant C\rho_0
\quad\hbox{on }B_{r+2\delta}\setminus B_r,
\end{equation}
where $C$ is an absolute constant. Define
\[
\rho_{r,\delta}(x)=
\begin{cases}
0,&|x|\leqslant r,\\
\rho_0+g_{r,\delta}(x),&r<|x|<r+2\delta,\\
\rho_0,&|x|\geqslant r+2\delta.
\end{cases}
\]
Then $\sqrt{\rho_{r,\delta}}$ is smooth and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:upper_collar_costs}
\int_{B_{r+2\delta}\setminus B_r}|\nabla\sqrt{\rho_{r,\delta}}|^2
\leqslant C\rho_0r^2/\delta,
\qquad
D(g_{r,\delta})\leqslant C\rho_0^2r^2\delta^3.
\end{equation}
The potential $\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}g_{r,\delta}(y)|x-y|^{-1}\,\mathrm dy$ vanishes for $|x|\geqslant r+2\delta$.
head: environment

label: eq:upper_collar_coefficient
title: Proof
body_md:
Choose fixed functions $\sigma,\vartheta\in C^\infty(\mathbb{R})$ such that
\[
0\leqslant \sigma\leqslant1,
\qquad \sigma(t)=0\ \hbox{for }t\leqslant\tfrac14,
\qquad \sigma(t)=1\ \hbox{for }t\geqslant\tfrac34,
\]
and
\[
\vartheta\geqslant0,
\qquad \operatorname{supp}\vartheta\subset(1,2),
\qquad I_\vartheta=\int_1^2\vartheta(t)\,\mathrm dt>0.
\]
For the ratio $\delta/r\leqslant1/2$, set
\begin{equation}\label{eq:upper_collar_coefficient}
 h(t)=\sigma(t)^2+c\vartheta(t),
 \qquad
 c=
 \frac{\displaystyle\int_0^2(1-\sigma(t)^2)(r+\delta t)^2\,\mathrm dt}
 {\displaystyle\int_1^2\vartheta(t)(r+\delta t)^2\,\mathrm dt}.
\end{equation}
The numerator is at least $r^2/4$, because $\sigma=0$ on $[0,1/4]$. It is at most $(r+\delta)^2\leqslant9r^2/4$, because $1-\sigma^2$ vanishes for $t\geqslant3/4$. The denominator lies between $r^2I_\vartheta$ and $(r+2\delta)^2I_\vartheta\leqslant4r^2I_\vartheta$. Consequently
\begin{equation}\label{eq:upper_collar_uniform_coefficient}
\frac1{16I_\vartheta}\leqslant c\leqslant\frac9{4I_\vartheta}.
\end{equation}
In particular, $0\leqslant h\leqslant C$ for an absolute constant $C$, and
\[
\sqrt{h(t)}=
\begin{cases}
\sigma(t),&0\leqslant t\leqslant1,\\
\sqrt{1+c\vartheta(t)},&1\leqslant t\leqslant2.
\end{cases}
\]
Both expressions are smooth, the second since $1+c\vartheta\geqslant1$. As $\operatorname{supp}\vartheta$ is a compact subset of $(1,2)$, $\vartheta$ vanishes near $t=1$ and near $t=2$. Since also $\sigma=1$ on $[3/4,1]$, both expressions equal one near $t=1$, so $\sqrt h$ is smooth on $[0,2]$. It vanishes for $t\leqslant1/4$ and equals one near $t=2$. Moreover,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:upper_collar_profile_gradient}
\int_0^2\big|(\sqrt h)'(t)\big|^2\,\mathrm dt
\leqslant\int_0^1|\sigma'(t)|^2\,\mathrm dt
+\frac14\left(\frac9{4I_\vartheta}\right)^2
\int_1^2|\vartheta'(t)|^2\,\mathrm dt
\leqslant C.
\end{equation}

Define
\[
g_{r,\delta}(x)=
\begin{cases}
\rho_0\left(h\left(\dfrac{|x|-r}{\delta}\right)-1\right),&r<|x|<r+2\delta,\\
0,&\hbox{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
The choice of $c$ implies
\[
\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}g_{r,\delta}
=4\pi\rho_0\delta\int_0^2(h(t)-1)(r+\delta t)^2\,\mathrm dt=0.
\]
The bound on the density follows from $0\leqslant h\leqslant C$. We have, by~\eqref{eq:upper_collar_profile_gradient},
\[
\int_{B_{r+2\delta}\setminus B_r}|\nabla\sqrt{\rho_{r,\delta}}|^2
=\frac{4\pi\rho_0}{\delta}
\int_0^2\big|(\sqrt h)'(t)\big|^2(r+\delta t)^2\,\mathrm dt
\leqslant C\rho_0r^2/\delta.
\]

To estimate the direct energy of $g_{r,\delta}$, let $Q(t)$ be the charge inside the sphere of radius $t$,
\[
Q(t)=4\pi\int_0^t s^2g_{r,\delta}(s)\,\mathrm ds.
\]
Its support as a function of $t$ is contained in $[r,r+2\delta]$, and
\[
|Q(t)|\leqslant\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}|g_{r,\delta}|
\leqslant C\rho_0r^2\delta.
\]
Since the total charge is zero, the potential $\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}g_{r,\delta}(y)|x-y|^{-1}\,\mathrm dy$ vanishes for $|x|\geqslant r+2\delta$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:basic_newton}(i). Theorem~\ref{thm:basic_newton}(iv) gives
\[
D(g_{r,\delta})
=\frac12\int_0^\infty\frac{Q(t)^2}{t^2}\,\mathrm dt
=\frac12\int_r^{r+2\delta}\frac{Q(t)^2}{t^2}\,\mathrm dt
\leqslant\delta\frac{\sup_tQ(t)^2}{r^2}
\leqslant C\rho_0^2r^2\delta^3.
\]
This proves the lemma.

label: lem:upper_packing
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:upper_packing}
Given $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, $\delta>0$ and $r_*>0$, there exist $L>0$ and finitely many balls $B_{r_m}(c_m)$, $1\leqslant m\leqslant M$, such that
\[
r_m\geqslant r_*\,,
\qquad N_m=\rho_0|B_{r_m}|\in\mathbb{N},
\qquad
\frac1{L^3}\sum_{m=1}^M|B_{r_m}|\geqslant1-\varepsilon,
\]
and the enlarged closed balls $\overline{B_{r_m+2\delta}(c_m)}$ are pairwise disjoint and contained in $C_L$.
head: environment
name: A finite packing with room for shells

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\mathcal{B}$ be the family of all closed balls $\overline{B_s(z)}$ with $s>0$ that are contained in the open unit cube $C_1$. It is a Vitali cover of $C_1$. Indeed, if $x\in C_1$ and $0<s<d(x,\partial C_1)$, then $\overline{B_s(x)}\in\mathcal{B}$, so every point of $C_1$ lies in balls of $\mathcal{B}$ of arbitrarily small radius. Since $\mathcal{B}$ consists of nondegenerate closed balls of diameter at most $1$, the Vitali covering theorem for Lebesgue measure~\cite[Sec.~1.5]{evans2015measure} applies. We obtain countably many pairwise disjoint balls $\overline{B_{s_k}(z_k)}\in\mathcal{B}$, $k\in\mathbb{N}$, such that $C_1\setminus\bigcup_k\overline{B_{s_k}(z_k)}$ is a null set. Since these balls are disjoint subsets of $C_1$,
\[
\sum_{k=1}^\infty|B_{s_k}|=|C_1|=1.
\]
Choose $M\geqslant2$ such that $\sum_{k=1}^M|B_{s_k}|>1-\varepsilon/2$. The balls $\overline{B_{s_m}(z_m)}$, $1\leqslant m\leqslant M$, are finitely many pairwise disjoint compact subsets of the open cube $C_1$. Hence
\[
d=\min\Big\{\min_{1\leqslant m<k\leqslant M}\big(|z_m-z_k|-s_m-s_k\big),\ \min_{1\leqslant m\leqslant M}\big(d(z_m,\partial C_1)-s_m\big)\Big\}>0.
\]

Next we dilate the cube $C_1$ and the balls $\overline{B_{s_m}(z_m)}$, $1\leqslant m\leqslant M$, by a large factor $L>0$. This gives the cube $C_L=LC_1$ and the balls $\overline{B_{Ls_m}(Lz_m)}$.
 We then round the radii $Ls_m$ down to neutral ones. For $1\leqslant m\leqslant M$ put
\[
N_m=\big\lfloor\rho_0|B_{Ls_m}|\big\rfloor,
\qquad
c_m=Lz_m,
\]
and let $r_m\geqslant0$ be the radius with $\rho_0|B_{r_m}|=N_m$. Then $r_m\leqslant Ls_m$. Since $N_m>\rho_0|B_{Ls_m}|-1$, we have
\[
|B_{r_m}|>|B_{Ls_m}|-\frac1{\rho_0}.
\]
In particular, $N_m\geqslant1$ and $r_m\geqslant r_*$ for all sufficiently large $L$. Summing over $m$ gives
\[
\frac1{L^3}\sum_{m=1}^M|B_{r_m}|
>\sum_{m=1}^M|B_{s_m}|-\frac{M}{\rho_0L^3}
>1-\frac\varepsilon2-\frac{M}{\rho_0L^3},
\]
which is at least $1-\varepsilon$ when $L^3\geqslant2M/(\rho_0\varepsilon)$. Finally, for $m\ne k$, the definition of $d$ and $r_m\leqslant Ls_m$ give
\[
|c_m-c_k|=L|z_m-z_k|\geqslant L(s_m+s_k+d)\geqslant r_m+r_k+Ld,
\]
so $\overline{B_{r_m+2\delta}(c_m)}$ and $\overline{B_{r_k+2\delta}(c_k)}$ are disjoint when $Ld>4\delta$. Similarly,
\[
d(c_m,\partial C_L)=L\,d(z_m,\partial C_1)\geqslant L(s_m+d)\geqslant r_m+Ld,
\]
so $\overline{B_{r_m+2\delta}(c_m)}\subset C_L$ when $Ld>2\delta$. See Figure~\ref{fig:packing}. Choosing $L$ large enough for all these conditions completes the proof.
head: environment

label: eq:upper_explicit_counting
title: Claim
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For the first assertion, consider the cells $a+Lz+C_L$, $z\in\mathbb{Z}^3$, which tile $\mathbb{R}^3$ up to null sets. The cell with index $z$ contains the balls $B_{r_m}(c_m+Lz+a)$, $1\leqslant m\leqslant M$, of total volume $\theta L^3$. Let
\[
Z_0=\{z\in\mathbb{Z}^3:\ a+Lz+\overline{C_L}\subset C_{\ell-2\delta}\},
\qquad
Z=\{z\in\mathbb{Z}^3:\ (a+Lz+C_L)\cap C_\ell\ne\emptyset\}.
\]
If $z\in Z_0$, then all enlarged balls of that cell lie in $C_{\ell-2\delta}$, so $(z,m)\in J_0(a,\ell)$ for every $m$. If $(z,m)\in J_0(a,\ell)$, then $B_{r_m}(c_m+Lz+a)\subset C_\ell$, so $z\in Z$. Hence
\[
\theta L^3|Z_0|\leqslant V(a,\ell)\leqslant\theta L^3|Z|.
\]
Two points of the closure of a cell differ by at most $L$ in each coordinate. Therefore every cell meeting $C_{\ell-2\delta-2L}$ has its index in $Z_0$, and every cell with index in $Z$ is contained in $C_{\ell+2L}$. Comparing volumes gives
\[
(\ell-2\delta-2L)^3\leqslant L^3|Z_0|,
\qquad
L^3|Z|\leqslant(\ell+2L)^3.
\]
Let $\ell\geqslant2(\delta+L)$. Using $(\ell-t)^3\geqslant \ell^3-3t\ell^2$ for $0\leqslant t\leqslant \ell$, $(\ell+2L)^3\leqslant \ell^3+26L\ell^2$ for $\ell\geqslant L$, and $\theta\leqslant1$, we obtain
\[
|V(a,\ell)-\theta \ell^3|\leqslant26(\delta+L)\ell^2,
\]
uniformly in $a\in C_L$. This proves the first assertion. Note that $\ell$ need not be a multiple of $L$, and the cells need not fit exactly into $C_\ell$. For the second, $|\partial B_r|=3|B_r|/r$ and $r_m\geqslant r_*$ give
\[
A(a,\ell)=\sum_{(z,m)\in J_0(a,\ell)}\frac{3|B_{r_m}|}{r_m}
\leqslant\frac3{r_*}V(a,\ell),
\]
and $V(a,\ell)\leqslant \ell^3$ because the selected balls are pairwise disjoint subsets of $C_\ell$.
head: environment
name: Proof of the claim

label: lem:LN_packing
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:LN_packing}
Let $p=26$ and $\gamma:=p/(1+p)=26/27$, and let $\mathcal B_k$, $k\geqslant0$, be the balls of radii $R_k=R_0\,27^k$ with $\rho_0|\mathcal B_0|=1$, so that $N_k:=\rho_0|\mathcal B_k|=27^{3k}$. For each $K\geqslant1$ the ball $\mathcal B_K$ contains pairwise disjoint balls, namely $n_{K-j}:=p^{K-j-1}(1+p)^{2(K-j)}$ translates of $\mathcal B_j$ for each $0\leqslant j\leqslant K-1$. The uncovered set $\mathcal D_K$ satisfies $|\mathcal D_K|=\gamma^K|\mathcal B_K|$, so that $M_K:=\rho_0|\mathcal D_K|=26^K\,27^{2K}\in\mathbb{N}$.

For the quantum problem we use the radii $R_k=R_0'(27^k-\frac12)$, still with $\rho_0|\mathcal B_0|=1$, so that $N_k=(2\cdot27^k-1)^3\in\mathbb{N}$. With the same multiplicities, the packing can then be chosen so that each packed ball is at distance at least $4h$ from $\partial \mathcal B_K$ and at least $8h$ from the other packed balls, where $h:=R_0'(1-\frac1{27})/8$. For this packing,
\[
M_K:=\rho_0|\mathcal D_K|=N_K-\sum_{j=0}^{K-1}n_{K-j}N_j\in\mathbb{N},
\]
and $|\mathcal D_K|/|\mathcal B_K|=\mathcal O(\gamma^K)$.
head: environment

label: lem:LN_trial
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:LN_trial}
For the quantum packing of Lemma~\ref{lem:LN_packing} there exist $C=C(\rho_0)$, independent of $K$, and normalized states $\Psi_K\in\bigwedge^{M_K}H^1_0(\mathcal D_K;\mathbb{C}^q)$ with
\[
\big\langle\Psi_K,H^{\rho_0}_{\mathcal D_K}\Psi_K\big\rangle\leqslant C\,|\mathcal D_K|.
\]
head: environment
name: Trial state on the leftover region

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) \emph{Penalization.} For $Y=(y_1,\ldots,y_{M_K})\in\mathcal D_K^{M_K}$, define
\[
U'(Y):=U^{\rho_0}_{\mathcal D_K}(Y)
+8\pi^2\sum_{1\leqslant i<j\leqslant M_K}\frac{\mathbb{1}_{\{|y_i-y_j|\leqslant1\}}}{|y_i-y_j|^2}.
\]
The added term penalizes close pairs and is integrable on $\mathcal D_K^{M_K}$.

(b) \emph{Keeping away from $\partial\mathcal D_K$.} Around each packed ball $\mathcal B^i$ (radius $R^i$) take the shells $S^i$ and $T^i$ of radii $(R^i,R^i+h)$ and $(R^i+h,R^i+2h)$, and inside $\partial \mathcal B_K$ the shells $S_K$ and $T_K$ of radii $(R_K-h,R_K)$ and $(R_K-2h,R_K-h)$. By the gaps in Lemma~\ref{lem:LN_packing}, all of them are disjoint and contained in $\mathcal D_K$. Let $f:=0$ on the $S$-shells, $f:=1+|S^i|/|T^i|$ on $T^i$, $f:=1+|S_K|/|T_K|$ on $T_K$ and $f:=1$ on the rest of $\mathcal D_K$, and extend $f$ by zero outside $\mathcal D_K$. Then $\int_{\mathcal D_K}f=|\mathcal D_K|$ and $f\leqslant3$.

(c) \emph{Averaging.} Integrate $U'$ over $\mathcal D_K^{M_K}$ against the product of the probability densities $f(y_i)/|\mathcal D_K|$. A direct computation gives
\[
\frac1{|\mathcal D_K|^{M_K}}\int_{\mathcal D_K^{M_K}}U^{\rho_0}_{\mathcal D_K}(Y)\prod_{i=1}^{M_K} f(y_i)\,\mathrm dY
=D\big(\rho_0(\mathbb{1}_{\mathcal D_K}-f)\big)-\frac{\rho_0}{|\mathcal D_K|}D(f)
\]
\cite[Eq.~(49)]{lieb1975thermodynamic}. Here $\rho_0(\mathbb{1}_{\mathcal D_K}-f)$ is a sum of neutral radial double layers $\tau^i$ (on $S^i\cup T^i$) and $\tau_K$ (on $S_K\cup T_K$). By Step~0 its self-energy is $\sum_iD(\tau^i)+D(\tau_K)\leqslant C\rho_0^2h^2|\mathcal D_K|$, because each double layer has energy of order $\rho_0^2h^2$ times its volume and all the shells lie in $\mathcal D_K$. Moreover,
\[
\frac{8\pi^2}{|\mathcal D_K|^{M_K}}\int_{\mathcal D_K^{M_K}}
\Bigg(\sum_{1\leqslant i<j\leqslant M_K}\frac{\mathbb{1}_{\{|y_i-y_j|\leqslant1\}}}{|y_i-y_j|^2}\Bigg)
\prod_{i=1}^{M_K} f(y_i)\,\mathrm dY
\leqslant C\rho_0M_K.
\]
Hence some $Y$ with all $y_i$ at distance $\geqslant h$ from $\partial\mathcal D_K$ satisfies $U'(Y)\leqslant C|\mathcal D_K|$.

(d) \emph{Orbitals.} Let
\begin{align*}
d_i&:=\frac12\min\{2h,1,\min_{j\ne i}|y_i-y_j|\},\\
\varphi_i(x)&=(2\pi d_i)^{-1/2}|x-y_i|^{-1}\sin(\pi|x-y_i|/d_i)\,\mathbb{1}_{B_{d_i}(y_i)}(x),
\end{align*}
where $\varphi_i$ is the Dirichlet ground state of the ball $B_{d_i}(y_i)\subset\mathcal D_K$. These balls are pairwise disjoint, so the Slater determinant $\Psi_K$ of the $\varphi_i$ (with any fixed spins) has the same energy as the Hartree product.

(e) \emph{Energy.} The kinetic energy satisfies
\begin{align*}
\sum_{i=1}^{M_K}\Big(\frac{\pi}{d_i}\Big)^2
&\leqslant8\pi^2\sum_{1\leqslant i<j\leqslant M_K}\frac{\mathbb{1}_{\{|y_i-y_j|\leqslant1\}}}{|y_i-y_j|^2}\\
&\quad+4\pi^2\max\{(2h)^{-2},1\}\,M_K.
\end{align*}
By Newton's theorem the pair interaction equals that of the point charges $y_i$. The background attraction decreases, since $V_{\mathcal D_K}$ is superharmonic, but per particle by at most
\[
\rho_0\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}\Big(\frac{1}{|z|}-\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}\frac{|\varphi_i(y_i+y)|^2}{|z-y|}\,\mathrm{d}y\Big)\,\mathrm{d}z=\xi\rho_0d_i^2,
\]
for a universal constant $\xi$. Altogether $\langle\Psi_K,H^{\rho_0}_{\mathcal D_K}\Psi_K\rangle\leqslant U'(Y)+C'M_K\leqslant C|\mathcal D_K|$.
head: environment
name: Sketch

label: lem:LN_sequences
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:LN_sequences}
Let $0<\gamma<1$ and let $(a_K)_{K\geqslant0}$ be a real sequence bounded below. Suppose that, for some $C\geqslant0$ and every $K\geqslant1$,
\[
a_K\leqslant(1-\gamma)\sum_{j=0}^{K-1}\gamma^{K-1-j}a_j+C\gamma^K.
\]
Then $(a_K)$ converges to a finite limit.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Set
\[
b_K:=(1-\gamma)\sum_{j=0}^{K-1}\gamma^{K-1-j}a_j+C\gamma^K.
\]
For $K\geqslant1$, the hypothesis gives
\[
b_{K+1}=\gamma b_K+(1-\gamma)a_K\leqslant b_K.
\]
Moreover, $b_K$ is bounded below, since it is a convex combination of $C,a_0,\ldots,a_{K-1}$. Thus $b_K\to b$ for some $b\in\mathbb{R}$, and
$a_K=\frac{b_{K+1}-\gamma b_K}{1-\gamma}\to b$.
head: environment

label: rem:LN_balls
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:LN_balls}
For every integer $N\geqslant1$, define $R_N$ by $\rho_0|B_{R_N}|=N$. The neutral balls $\Omega_N=B_{R_N}$ form an LN-admissible sequence. Conditions (A) and (B) are clear, and (i) holds because $|\Sigma^{+1}_{N,h}|\leqslant|\Sigma^{+2}_{N,h}|$. For each fixed $h>0$, $R_N\geqslant4h$ holds for all sufficiently large $N$, so $|\Sigma^{-2}_{N,h}|>0$ on this tail. Moreover, $R_N\geqslant4h$ holds for every $N\geqslant1$ once $4h<R_1$, as required for the uniform estimate in~(ii). Under this condition the double layers are radial about the origin, neutral, bounded by $4$, and supported in $\{R_N\leqslant|x|\leqslant R_N+2h\}$ and $\{R_N-2h\leqslant|x|\leqslant R_N\}$, respectively. For $0<|x|\leqslant R_N+2h$ put $m=\max\{|x|,R_N\}$. Newton's formula~\eqref{eq:basic_newton} and neutrality give
\[
\varphi_{N,h}(x)=4\pi\int_m^{R_N+2h}\sigma^+_{N,h}(s)\,s\Big(1-\frac sm\Big)\,\mathrm ds.
\]
Since $0\leqslant s/m-1\leqslant2h/R_N$ in the integral, $|\varphi_{N,h}(x)|\leqslant16\pi h^2(1+2h/R_N)\leqslant24\pi h^2$, which is (ii). Finally, the charge of either double layer inside the sphere of radius $t$ vanishes for $t$ outside an interval of length $2h$ contained in $[R_N/2,\infty)$, and it is at most $CR_N^2h$ in absolute value. Hence Theorem~\ref{thm:basic_newton}(iv) gives $D(\sigma^+_{N,h}),D(\sigma^-_{N,h})\leqslant CR_N^2h^3=o(|\Omega_N|)$, which is (iii) and (iv).
